cases.claim: [P2] `src/StaticAssets/src/Development/StaticAssetDevelopmentRuntimeHandler.cs:65` — Deleting or renaming an uncompressed source asset in Development still serves its stale precompressed `.gz`/`.br` artifact instead of returning `404 Not Found`.
cases.effect: For compressed endpoints (`asset.HasContentEncoding()`), `AttachRuntimePatching` resolves `asset` to `originalAsset` (the uncompressed source file in `wwwroot`), whereas the inner `StaticAssetsInvoker` holds `_resource` pointing to the build-generated `.gz`/`.br` artifact (which in `dotnet run` lives under `obj/.../compressed/`). Guarding the metadata check with `if (fileInfo.Exists && ...)` (and swallowing `FileNotFoundException` at lines 75–78) causes a deleted `wwwroot` source file to fall through to `original(context)`, where `StaticAssetsInvoker.EnsureFileExists()` checks `_resource.AssetPath` (`.gz`/`.br`), finds it still on disk, and responds `200 OK` (or `304 Not Modified`) with the stale compressed asset instead of `404 Not Found` with `Cache-Control: no-store`.
cases.repro: ```csharp CreateTestManifest(appName, webRoot, [new TestResource("sample.txt", "Hello, World!", IncludeCompressedVersion: true)]); await using var app = await StartMissingAssetTestAppAsync(appName, contentRoot, webRoot, reloadStaticAssetsAtRuntime: true); using var client = app.GetTestClient(); File.Delete(Path.Combine(webRoot, "sample.txt")); // delete source file in wwwroot while build-generated .gz remains using var request = new HttpRequestMessage(HttpMethod.Get, "/sample.txt"); request.Headers.AcceptEncoding.Add(new StringWithQualityHeaderValue("gzip")); using var response = await client.SendAsync(request); // Returns 200 OK instead of 404 Not Found

cases.head: 3a579bae63c05935d03a5f8b336fc4c8e69a2389
cases.claim: Promoting this wrapper creates duplicate Error records for circuit-handler failures
cases.effect:
`src/Components/Server/src/Circuits/CircuitHost.cs:1042` · [severity removed]
**Minimal repro:** Register a `CircuitHandler` whose `OnCircuitOpenedAsync` throws, then start an Interactive Server circuit.
`OnCircuitOpenedAsync` already logs `CircuitHandlerFailed` at Error before rethrowing an aggregate; `InitializeAsync` now logs the same failure again as `InitializationFailed` at Error. The first-update path similarly duplicates it through `UpdateRootComponentsFailed`.

cases.head: 66e5ff9a216147eda5eb6d57f6f0d31d0951f524
cases.claim: `ItemsProvider_ThrowsAfterPartialResults_ExceptionCaptured` never invokes the throwing second provider call and asserts the opposite of exception capture
cases.effect: 1. The first `callbacks.OnAfterSpacerVisible(0f, 500f, 500f, ...)` sets `_visibleItemCapacity = 40`, `_itemsBefore = 0`, invokes `partiallyThrowingProvider` once (`callCount == 1`), and sets `_itemCount = 100` and `_skipNextDistributionRefresh = true`. 2. The second `callbacks.OnAfterSpacerVisible(5000f, 500f, 500f, ...)` never calls `partiallyThrowingProvider` (`callCount` remains `1`): with `SpacerVisibilityReason.ViewportFill`, `Virtualize.OnAfterSpacerVisible` (`Virtualize.cs:879-883`) short-circuits on `_skipNextDistributionRefresh`; even with `SpacerVisibilityReason.IntersectionEvent`, `spacerSize = 5000f` computes `itemsAfter = Math.Max(0, 5000/50 - 15) = 85` and `itemsBefore = Math.Max(0, 100 - 85 - 40) = 0 == _itemsBefore` while `_lastRenderedItemCount == 0` (since `CreateRenderedVirtualize` passes `childContent: null`), so `UpdateItemDistribution` (`Virtualize.cs:953`) skips `RefreshDataCoreAsync`.
cases.repro: Fix the 4-argument `OnAfterSpacerVisible` signature and run `ItemsProvider_ThrowsAfterPartialResults_ExceptionCaptured`, then either assert `callCount == 2` or change the second callback's arguments so `UpdateItemDistribution` actually refreshes.

cases.head: 1f7c0bc1a75742850ee7636b40666e5ca0b538c3
cases.claim: On multithreaded Interactive WebAssembly, the new off-renderer `InvokeAsync(Func<Task>)` path changes an asynchronous `ItemsProvider` failure from its original exception type to `AggregateException`.
cases.effect: The changed line enters `WebAssemblyDispatcher.InvokeAsync(Func<Task>)`; its fault forwarding calls `state.tcs.SetException(t.Exception)` where `t.Exception` is already an `AggregateException`. Awaiting the returned task therefore throws that aggregate instead of the provider exception, breaking callers that handle the documented provider failure type. The old code directly awaited `RefreshDataCoreAsync`, so this pure-provider failure surfaced as the original exception before `StateHasChanged` was reached.
cases.repro: Configure a non-virtualized QuickGrid `ItemsProvider` that asynchronously throws `InvalidOperationException`. From a timer/worker callback in multithreaded Interactive WebAssembly, call and await `grid.RefreshDataAsync()` inside `catch (InvalidOperationException)`. The catch no longer runs; the awaited call throws `AggregateException` whose inner exception is the provider's `InvalidOperationException`.

cases.head: 39b01416d015e6dda10381a4cb4a1487ac9bee80
cases.claim: [P2] Do not make root removal wait for initial-render quiescence.
cases.effect: the Remove (and replacement Add) waits behind the first batch, which awaits Slow's initialization/quiescence. Dispose is the operation that completes that initialization, so it never runs; subsequent page roots cannot become interactive on this circuit. Causal/frozen evidence: head CircuitHost.cs:840 waits previousUpdate; :847 waits dispatcher processing; :930-934 awaits PerformRootComponentOperations; :1012-1014 awaits initial pending tasks; updateCompletion is resolved only in the enclosing finally. Shared/src/WebRootComponentManager.cs:36-59 registers the root before awaiting RenderAsync; Renderer.cs:321-343 waits component quiescence, and ComponentBase.cs:260-309 awaits OnInitializedAsync. Browser WebRootComponentManager.ts:396-466 produces Remove when the descriptor leaves the document even while Add remains unacknowledged, and :332-343 sends batches without waiting for earlier acknowledgements; CircuitManager.ts:98-104 sends to ComponentHub.cs:188-237, which fire-and-forgets each host update. In merge-base and base-tip, each update is independently dispatched, so Remove runs while initialization is suspended. WebRootComponentManager.RemoveRootComponent -> WebRootComponent.Remove -> Renderer.RemoveRootComponent (:352-369) -> ProcessRenderQueue/ProcessDisposalQueueInExistingBatch -> ComponentState.DisposeAsync (:334-356) invokes Dispose, canceling initialization and permitting completion. Head prevents this path from being reached. This is separate from the dispatcher remaining reentrant. Fix direction: separate successor readiness after handlers/setup/root operations have actually been established from completion of asynchronous initial component quiescence. Keep required initialization ordering, but do not gate removal on the lifecycle operation that removal must cancel. A safe complete patch is not a one-line change, so no speculative fix snippet is supplied.

cases.head: 39b01416d015e6dda10381a4cb4a1487ac9bee80
cases.claim: [P2] Start the overflow error notification before raising the teardown event.
cases.effect: batch 11 enters the new overflow path and terminates the circuit, but the intended JS.Error notification is always skipped with the normal CircuitRegistry subscriber. The browser does not immediately receive this path's fatal-error notification and the queued parameter updates/acknowledgements are lost. Causal/frozen evidence: same-key descriptors merge and change uniqueId in DomSync.ts:174-186 and ComponentDescriptorDiscovery.ts:342-367. NavigationEnhancement.ts:345-351 clears performingEnhancedPageLoad before enhancedNavigationCompleted; WebRootComponentManager.ts:439-451 emits each changed descriptor update. Old manager has already registered the root ID before initial quiescence; matching-key UpdateAsync accepts these updates, and old CircuitHost acknowledges each without awaiting subsequent render quiescence. Head reserves ten pending slots and rejects the eleventh. cases.head: 39b01416d015e6dda10381a4cb4a1487ac9bee80
cases.claim: `ReportRootComponentUpdateQueueOverflowAsync` invokes `UnhandledException` before `TryNotifyClientErrorAsync`, causing `CircuitRegistry` to synchronously set `Client.Connected = false` and suppress the `"JS.Error"` notification to the browser.
cases.effect: `UnhandledException?.Invoke(...)` synchronously runs `CircuitRegistry.CircuitHost_UnhandledException` -> `TerminateAsync(circuitHost.CircuitId)`, which calls `circuitHost.Client.SetDisconnected()` (`Client.Connected = false`) before yielding at `await circuitHost.DisposeAsync()`. When `await TryNotifyClientErrorAsync(Client, GetClientErrorMessage(exception), exception)` executes on the next line, `TryNotifyClientErrorAsync` sees `!Client.Connected` (`CircuitHost.cs:742`), logs `UnhandledExceptionClientDisconnected`, and returns without sending `"JS.Error"`, so the browser client never runs `CircuitManager.unhandledError` (`showErrorNotification()` / `connection.stop()`).
cases.repro: Register a `CircuitHandler` whose `OnCircuitOpenedAsync` awaits a pending task (keeping `_initialized == false`), register the `CircuitHost` with `CircuitRegistry` (as `ComponentHub.StartCircuit` does in production), and enqueue 101 `UpdateRootComponents` calls to trigger the pending queue overflow.

cases.head: 2edf3761692afe15475075eb2fc0088566162045
cases.claim: Concurrent requests can use different invalidation tokens, allowing a stale result to remain cacheable.
cases.effect:
Only the CTS still stored in `_authenticationStateChangedCts` is canceled. The other request sees an uncanceled token at line 77 and writes its stale token into `_lastToken` and `_cachedHeader`, defeating the fix.
Fix: synchronize CTS acquisition, authentication-state invalidation, and the cancellation-check/cache commit using the same lock, or use an equivalent atomic generation mechanism that makes the check and commit indivisible relative to invalidation.
cases.repro: Issue two concurrent authorized requests while the cache is empty. If both evaluate the unsynchronized `??=` before either assignment is visible, each can retain a different CTS token. Raise `AuthenticationStateChanged`, then complete the request whose CTS was overwritten with an old token.
